captures.q: Tell me about the arguments and speculative implications of Lee Sharks' Whose Face Is on the Twenty?
captures.description: THE OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: the essay 'investigates the visual presentation of the portrait on the redesigned United States $20 bill, arguing that the modern curatorial and aesthetic choices made during the currency's redesign process unintentionally or intentionally unmasked a stark, latent resemblance between the engraved portrait and Jeffrey Epstein.' The core arguments (the Welch engraving; the redesign's unidirectional effect; feature legibility; the curatorial gap) and the speculative implications, 'Tier D' (awareness in the redesign; the officials' 'documented real-world ties to Epstein'). Two cards, both Medium (Lee Sharks).

captures.q: Tell me about the arguments and speculative implications of Lee Sharks' Whose Face Is on the Twenty?
captures.description: CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The essay advances a provocative visual hypothesis: that the redesigned portrait of Andrew Jackson bears a striking resemblance to Jeffrey Epstein, and that institutional decisions about the presentation of the portrait made that resemblance more visible.' Seven sections: the central argument (same engraving, different face; five features; latent feature activation); the institutional argument (Sully, Welch, the 1928 master die, the 1996 redesign; Rubin, Summers; the curatorial gap); five counterarguments; speculative implications (intentional, negligent, accidental); the companion essay, The Lizard People Were Right; a critical assessment; the larger significance. It closes: 'I would take the institutional and philosophical questions seriously while withholding judgment on the Epstein resemblance and any suggestion of deliberate involvement.'
